Venezuelan Oil Sector Sees Boost With New Investment in Zulia State

MARACAIBO — The oil-rich region of Zulia is set to benefit from a significant new investment in Venezuela’s oil and gas sector, industry officials announced on Thursday. PetroAndina, a leading energy producer in the country, has revealed plans to expand its crude extraction operations in the Lagunillas municipality, promising to inject new momentum into Venezuela’s efforts to revive its energy output.

According to company spokesperson Luis Vargas, the expansion is expected to bring an estimated $150 million in capital expenditure over the next two years. “This is an important step for both PetroAndina and the communities of Zulia. We are committed to increasing production capacity while supporting local employment and development,” Vargas said at a press conference in Maracaibo.

The project will focus on the installation of new drilling platforms and the modernization of existing infrastructure. Company officials estimate that the initiative could create up to 350 direct jobs and several hundred more in supporting sectors such as transportation, catering, and equipment maintenance.

Energy Minister María del Rosario hailed the announcement, saying, “The government welcomes this investment, which aligns with our strategy to revitalize Venezuela’s oil industry and ensure sustainable growth for our regions. We look forward to the positive impact on our communities.”

Local trade union representative Jorge Parra expressed optimism regarding job creation, noting, “This expansion offers hope to many families in Lagunillas. We expect transparent hiring practices and good working conditions for our members.”

Industry analysts suggest that, while challenges remain for Venezuela’s oil sector, targeted investments such as this could help stabilize output and attract further interest in the country’s vast energy resources.

Work on the new facilities is scheduled to begin in the third quarter of this year, with full operational capacity anticipated by late 2025.
